_comment: Shared drift vectors for the dual-homed assessment/subject.py normalize_subdir
(extraction spec 6.4). This file is byte-identical in CodeRoot-OpenSource and
CodeRoot-Repo-Assessor; both suites assert it, so a divergent copy fails loudly.
DERIVED BY EXECUTION, not from a design sketch: every entry below was run through
the implementation and records what it actually returned. Two inputs a design
sketch predicted would be REJECTED are in fact accepted -- '/absolute' and the
UNC-style backslash path -- and are recorded as accepts here. A '.' path segment
is COLLAPSED (like an empty segment already was), not left in place: 'pkg/./a'
normalizes to 'pkg/a', the same subject as 'pkg/a' itself -- a bare '.' segment
surviving normalization used to mint a second, unreachable asset_id for the same
directory and filter its content to nothing (adversarial review finding 2).
The reject list is the security-relevant half: normalize_subdir is the canonical
validation gate for an attacker-supplied subdir on CodeRoot's request path.
